public_rationale: OpenAI's September 5, 2025 explanation explicitly says hallucinations are not inevitable because models can abstain when uncertain [e1]. Its accompanying paper limits inevitability to base models under its assumptions and describes a non-hallucinating system that uses a database and calculator for restricted questions and otherwise abstains [e2]. These exceptions contradict the attribution to OpenAI of mathematical inevitability regardless of harnesses or scripts [e1] [e2].
limitations: The assertions about thoughts and knowledge remain unassessed; the cited findings concern hallucination and abstention [e1] [e2].
The restricted-system example does not establish that useful, open-ended assistants can answer every question without hallucinating [e2].

statement.excerpt: It does not have thoughts, or “knowledge,” and no matter how many layers of harnesses and scripts you put on top of it, it is still (per OpenAI) mathematically certain to hallucinate.

from_speaker: no matter how many layers of harnesses and scripts
our_interpretation: The checkable commitment is that OpenAI established a mathematical inevitability result covering generative AI even with external harnesses and scripts.
I read mathematically certain as a universal result under the claimed scope, not merely evidence that current systems sometimes hallucinate.
The target is the content of the cited OpenAI research, publicly released September 5, 2025, as invoked by the July 2026 post.
Thoughts and knowledge have no supplied operational meanings. The assessment does not infer consciousness or its absence from hallucination research.
The categorical mathematical attribution can be contradicted without resolving the separate philosophical language.
criteria.support_condition: OpenAI's published result establishes unavoidable hallucination for the full claimed class, including systems allowed to abstain or constrain outputs through external controls.
criteria.contradiction_condition: OpenAI's result explicitly allows non-hallucinating systems or limits inevitability to assumptions that do not cover all post-training methods, harnesses, and scripts.
